name: @playliquid/runtime-spark
description: PlayLiquid GameOS Spark runtime (PL-035). A THIN fast-start shell over the merged runtime-core kernel (PL-013, never a fork): the deterministic boot pipeline materializes the MINIMAL first-interaction world state from game-ir content — a typed boot PLAN (what loads now vs what streams later) derived from the FROZEN SparkTargetProfile boot budgets (firstPaintTargetMs/firstInteractionTargetMs as PLANNING inputs under an injected clock and an explicit caller-supplied cost model, E9 — no platform policy numbers are invented here), the 9:16 portrait viewport projection (R6, pure math — PL-033's game-ui owns presentation), and the deferred/streamed remainder as typed digest-pinned descriptors. Boot is TOTAL: invalid content/profile inputs are typed kebab-case refusals accumulated in ONE pass. Progressive streaming (typed, priority-ordered, content-derived schedules; cycle and contradiction refusals) plus aggressive caching (content-addressed, digest-pinned admission model with cache-rule violation refusals). First-interaction discipline: the interaction-ready transition (boot plan applied → first command accepted) is witnessed by an immutable SparkBootRecord (E10) carrying the plan digest, the accepted-first-command digest and the deterministic ordering. Tenancy (R20): runtime instances are tenant-scoped and cross-tenant access is a typed refusal. No real network (E11): the IO seams are pure ports; the in-repo implementations are deterministic fakes. Spark is a TARGET PROFILE, not a second content model (lock rule 16): all content comes from game-ir, all profile data from runtime-contracts' SparkTargetProfile.
